TDD · Sindri · #2258

Say it in one sentence to an agent, and the workflow exists and runs.

Sindri drops recipes, the factory pipeline and approvals. In their place: workflows as graphs of generic blocks, built over MCP, plus connections, memory, toolkits and resources an agent can set up without anyone opening the app.

Part 1

Why Sindri changes

Sindri, agent-first3 / 34
1.1 · The problem today

Small automations are impossible to build today

The everyday work that keeps a team moving is trigger → agent → condition → notify. Sindri can't express it without new code.

1

Blocks know their station

step.scope.*, step.lens.round and the line dispatcher only make sense inside the one pipeline, so nothing is reusable.

2

Every change waits for a human

Profile edits, recipes and pins sit until sindri profile approve <hash> is typed in a human terminal.

3

Agents are locked out

Agent sessions are refused at 89 call sites, so an agent can't build or run what it was asked to.

4

The pipeline never worked

Intake → scoping → design → build → prove → ship was too ambitious to be reliable.

The everyday work that keeps a team moving is trigger → agent → condition → notify. Sindri can't express it without new code.
1.2 · Why it keeps happening

Five whys, from "I can't automate this" to the root

Symptom

A nightly drift check that opens a PR can't be built in Sindri.

Why 1

No block means "start an agent in repo X with this prompt".Agent runs exist only inside line Steps (docs/csharp/sindri-workflow.md Agent runtime P8)

Why 2

Blocks were designed for stations, not for reuse.Block catalogs are per station: scoping, design, plan, build, prove

Why 3

Every new recipe needs approval and often new C#.recipe approve, profile approve, SND-AUTH-002 × 89

Root

The engine models one pipeline, not a set of generic steps an agent can wire together.

Sindri, agent-first5 / 34
1.3 · How we solve it

Make a workflow a graph of generic blocks that an agent builds over MCP, and trust the editor.

1 · Trust

No approvals, every verb

Edits apply on save after validation; agent sessions can do anything a human terminal can, with attribution.

Profile, auth, ledger
2 · Engine

Graph workflows on Temporal

One GraphWorkflow interprets every spec; run_agent launches a sandboxed session.

New Graph slice, launcher
3 · Platform

Connections, memory, toolkits, resources

Sign in once, remember across runs, add C# tools, declare a database or disk.

New slices + MCP tools
Sindri, agent-first6 / 34
1.3 · How we solve it

What we are not building

What we are not building

  • A hosted relay or public webhooks
  • Multi-user sharing
  • A port of the factory pipeline

What we build instead

  • Polling triggers with catch-up on wake
  • A generic pull inbox for outside systems
  • A canvas in the app, last

2.5 · Lifecycle

A run's status only moves forward

queuedwaiting its turn
runningwalking nodes
waitingagent report or an answer
succeeded
failed
cancelled
run id = <workflow>@<revision>:<occurrence>; a second start with the same id is refused
  • engine Start → running
  • node run_agent or ask_owner → waiting
  • session Report or answer → running
  • engine Last node done → succeeded
  • engine Node failed (stop) → failed
  • anyone Cancel → cancelled

4.2 · Build plan

Eight milestones, each proven before the next

1

M1 · Trust (PR1-2)

Profile edits apply on save; every verb open to sessions with attribution.

parallel with M2
2

M2 · Clear the ground (PR3-4)

Delete recipes, the line, their pages, schemas and docs; keep items, ledger, launcher, sandbox.

3

M3 · Graph engine (PR5-7)

Spec, validator, GraphWorkflow, run store, core blocks and run_agent.

4

M4 · Agent-first building (PR8-9)

MCP build tools and docs; the first workflow ships at PR8.

5

M5 · Connections (PR10-12)

Four kinds, sign-in, refresh, polling with catch-up, the handoff inbox.
